claim: Bulk-tissue RNA (HPA consensus, 40 tissues) confines CEACAM5 signal to GI-mucosal tissue (colon 920.3, rectum 885.1, appendix 175.2, stomach 154.1, esophagus 148.8 nTPM); lung is the one non-GI compartment with a non-trivial value (28.5 nTPM, above small intestine's 23.2) not strongly corroborated by GTEx (4.6 median TPM) -- flagged as worth a protein/IHC check, not resolved here. Liver/heart/kidney/bone marrow all <1 nTPM.
notes: GI-mucosal-confined pattern matches known CEACAM5/CEA biology, not a new liability; cannot conclude a therapeutic window (see module README Cannot-prove). Bulk RNA only -- the registered HPA_normal_tissue dataset's IHC/cell-type-resolved component is not part of this row.

claim: GTEx v11 median TPM (68 tissues) corroborates the HPA GI-mucosal pattern at the subregion level: Colon_Transverse_Mucosa 1069.6 vs Colon_Transverse_Muscularis 75.4 (>10x), Esophagus_Mucosa 277.8 vs Esophagus_Muscularis 0.14 (>1000x) -- signal tracks epithelial content specifically, not whole-organ. Colon_Sigmoid (0.74) vs Colon_Transverse (243.7) is an unexplained within-organ discrepancy in this source, recorded as open, not resolved by assumption. Liver/heart/kidney all <0.1 median TPM; GTEx v11 has no bone marrow tissue.
notes: REFERENCE_SUPPORT tier per module_classification.tsv -- catches normal-organ signal HPA might miss, cannot alone establish a safety conclusion. nTPM (HPA) and median_TPM (GTEx) are not directly comparable across rows TE001/TE002; each source's pattern is read within itself, not cross-normalized.
